title: I, Ball
build: one-file whole-memory image, $0314-$FFFF, started by an IRQ hook at $033C (I_Ball.prg, MD5 ab57fa0a25cfa9ab7b411317f9a305ca); from the OneLoad64 games collection v5; original release unknown

accuracy.note: 60 hand-written and 20 generated comments, from 647 and 166, checked by a fresh agent against the code; 19 others that shared the wrong ones' beliefs were corrected with them

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's variables (named in the listing) and the music driver's pointers
system: the KERNAL's work area, which the game does not use once it runs
system: the rest of the cassette buffer and the KERNAL's vectors after start_hook
runtime: the screen and the sprite pointers, written by clear_screen, draw_playfield and the text routines
never read: the RAM's power-on pattern ($00 and $FF in blocks) and zeros

runtime: the map buffer, built from the level's tile list by build_level_map at the start of every level (at the hand-over it holds a map, and at $1FB3 the text SEARCHING LOADING BLOCK? REWIND TO, which the build overwrites); the last two bytes are never written or read
runtime: the shot table and the variables after it, cleared by new_game and reset_level; at the hand-over they hold leftover code
runtime: the per-sprite sets and the extras flags; at the hand-over they hold leftover code
never read: zeros, with seven stray bytes at $70A7
never read: the RAM's power-on pattern, with leftovers of a loader at $8CD0-$8DFF (code that copies memory and sets up the screen, and two lines of text), which the game never runs
runtime: the high-nybble table, built by make_nybble_table before every sample
never read: the RAM's power-on pattern

never read: RAM under the I/O area, which the game never banks in for the processor and the video chip (bank 0) cannot see. $D000-$D3FF holds what looks like map rows, left from before the image was saved; the rest is the RAM's power-on pattern
never read: leftovers after the effects' definitions, which no pointer reaches: four-bit data like the speech samples', multicolour graphics, and at $FF00 the text **LOADING 12
runtime: the hardware NMI and IRQ vectors, written by set_sample_nmi and the interrupt handlers
extra: the sprite shapes $80-$BF: the panels' icons, timer digits, score and meter sprites, Iball's roll, the aliens, the disc, the explosions and the pieces
the playfield's character set, which the video chip reads through $D018 (the animated characters at $36F0 and the dot at $37F8 are rewritten in play)
the text character set of the title and the screens between levels, with the sprite shapes $E0-$FF above it: the lives, the friends and the explosion

regions: the text character set and sprites $E0-$FF
the shot table, the random table and the flags
three frames of the animated characters
the speech player and its test program
the music: patterns, instruments and tracks
the sound effects' scripts and definitions
